svg.title: Two durable handoffs, one stable recipient/channel identity
svg.desc: The order database commits OrderReady O847 version 9 and its business outbox together. A relay retries that event into notification ingest. A notification transaction deduplicates the event and creates N501, email/push deliveries and a delivery outbox together. Repeated publication retains the same delivery ID in the channel queue. Workers claim the row and call the provider separately. Neither transaction nor queue acknowledgement is proof that a provider delivered a message or that the customer read it.
svg.text: A durable event is not a delivered message
OrderReady/O847/v9 → customer U21 → inbox N501 + optional email/push work.
Transaction 1 · order authority
Order state = READY and business outbox E9 commit together.
Crash before commit: neither. Crash after commit: relay can recover E9.
retry same event ID + payload
Transaction 2 · notification authority
Deduplicate E9 → inbox N501 + D-email + D-push + delivery outbox.
Only after commit: 202 ACCEPTED. A retry returns the same acceptance result.
No provider is called under this transaction. Channel work may still be queued, delayed or suppressed.
publication can repeat
Email / push queues
Each copy points to the original delivery ID.
Broker acknowledgement ≠ worker completion.
Claimed worker → provider
Fresh permission + immutable provider key
Remote outcome can still be uncertain.
Keep these facts separate
Business committed → accepted → enqueued → provider accepted → delivery evidence
User read is an independent authenticated application fact, not the final queue state.
